verses.text: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to test Jesus. “Show us a sign from heaven,” they said.
He answered, “At sunset you say, ‘The sky’s red, so tomorrow’s weather will be good.’”
“And in the morning, ‘The sky’s red and threatening, so bad weather’s coming.’ Hypocrites! You know how to read the sky, but you can’t read the signs of the times!”
“An evil, unfaithful generation keeps asking for a sign. It won’t get one except the sign of Jonah.” Then he left them and went away.
The disciples reached the other side and realized they’d forgotten to bring bread.
Jesus told them, “Watch out. Stay alert for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
They started talking among themselves: “He says that because we didn’t bring bread.”
Jesus knew what they were saying. “Why are you all talking about having no bread? You have so little faith!”
“Don’t you get it yet? Remember the five loaves for five thousand people—and how many baskets you picked up afterward?”
“Or the seven loaves for four thousand—and how many baskets you picked up then?”
“How are you missing that I wasn’t talking about bread? Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then they understood: he wasn’t warning them about bread yeast, but about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came to the area around Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say I, the Son of Man, am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptizer; some say Elijah; others say Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He asked them, “But who do you say I am?”
Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered him, “You’re blessed, Simon son of Jonah, because no human being revealed this to you. My Father in heaven did.”
“I’m telling you: you are Peter, and on this rock I’ll build my church. The gates of Hades won’t overpower it.”
“I’ll give you the keys to Heaven’s Kingdom. Whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.” 🗝️
Then he strictly warned his disciples not to tell anyone he was the Christ.

From then on, Jesus began explaining to his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and teachers of the Law, be killed, and be raised on the third day.
Peter pulled him aside and started rebuking him: “No way, Lord! This won’t happen to you.”
But Jesus turned and told Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You’re tripping me up. You’re focused on human things, not God’s things.”
Then Jesus told his disciples, “If anyone wants to follow me, they must deny themselves, pick up their cross, and come with me.”
“Whoever tries to save their life will lose it; whoever loses their life for my sake will find it.”
“What do you gain if you get the whole world but lose your life? What could anyone trade for their life?”
“The Son of Man will come in his Father’s glory with his angels, and then he’ll repay each person according to what they’ve done.”
“I’m telling you the truth: some standing here won’t die before they see the Son of Man coming in his Kingdom.”
